questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order.

A. I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest.

B. When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right.

C. My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly.

D. His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'BADC'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Whenever we try to arrange the sequence of the jumbled sentences, it's important to find out the first sentence.
 
• The sentence **'B'** is the **first **one as it explains the situation perfectly. ***(When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right.)***
 
• The **second **in the sequence would be the sentence **'A' **that states what I saw beneath the tree. ***(I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest.**)***
 
• The **third** in the sequence would be the sentence **'D' **that tells about the condition of that middle-aged man. ***(His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.)***
 
• 
 The sentence **'C' **is the **last **one as it talks about how I felt at the end. ***( My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly.)***
 

***​***Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's understand some important words given in the sentences.
 
• **Shiver (verb) - to shake slightly or quickly because of feeling cold, ill, or frightened** - *She was **shivering **with the cold that's why she covered herself with the blanket.*
 
• **Bitterly (adverb) - in a way that shows deep anger and pain** - *He was **bitterly **disappointed when he couldn't get through the exam.*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The yoga instructor said to us, “Doing yoga daily will help you to develop a healthy mind and body."

options.text: The yoga instructor was told them that daily yoga would help them to develop a healthy mind and body
The yoga instructor said to us that doing daily yoga will be helping us to develop a healthy mind and body
The yoga instructor told us that doing yoga daily would help us to develop a healthy mind and body.
The yoga instructor said to us that daily yoga will help us to develop a healthy mind and body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'The yoga instructor told us that doing yoga daily would help us to develop a healthy mind and body.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Follow some basic rules, whenever you have to convert the speech from **direct to indirect.**

__
 
• In the first part of the sentence (reporting speech), remember to **change the verb according to the tense.**
 
• Remove inverted commas using **'that'.**
 
• In the second part of the sentence (reported speech), remember to **change the verb according to the tense of the first part of the sentence** (reporting speech)

On the basis of the above rules,** change 'said to' into 'told' and 'will' into would'** as the sentence is in the past tense.

The indirect speech would be *'the yoga instructor told us that doing yoga daily would help us to develop a healthy mind and body.'*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's understand the concept with some more examples

 
• Patrick said to Sara, "I will meet you in the restaurant."
 
 
• *Patrick told Sara that he would meet her in the restaurant.*
 
 
 
• She said to me, "I will help you in English."
 
 
• *She told me that she would help me in English.*

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Start **the sentence **with the object**. (*All the topics in the syllabus - 'object')*
 
• If a **modal **is used in the sentence, use **'be + verb 3rd form' with the given model**. (*should be covered - 'be + verb 3rd form')*
 
• In the **end**, use **'by + subject (doer)'** in order to show the relation between the action and subject. (*by teachers - 'by + subject or doer')*

Now if we follow the above rules, the sentence will be:

 
• *All the topics in the syllabus should be covered by teachers*

*​*Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Let's understand the concept with some more examples.

• **How much - **can be used with **an uncountable noun - sugar, time, money, milk, etc.** - ***How much time** will you take to get ready?*
 
• **How much - **can be used with** a countable noun to know the price - dress, jacket, etc. **- ***How much** is this **jacket**?*
